pricing_model.quote: Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API

name: Muse Spark
tagline: Meta's general multimodal model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Meta's general model for new projects on the Model API (muse-spark-1.3), with Standard and Contributor tiers. Trained for agentic, long-horizon work with tool calling; perceives video, images and documents.
how_it_helps: Use it to read documents and images, draft and summarise text, extract structured data, or plan a build, by calling the API with the OpenAI SDK.
pros: Meta's general model for new projects, with Standard and pay-less Contributor tiers.
Works with the OpenAI Python SDK by changing the base URL and key.
Supports structured JSON output and tool calling.
cons: For speech transcription use Muse Voice Transcribe, not this model.
Reasoning tokens count against max_output_tokens, so set generous budgets.
Confirm regional availability for your account with a test call.

prompt_style.technique: State the task, give the input, and say the exact output format you want.
prompt_style.format: Plain-language instruction followed by the input; ask for JSON when you need structured output.
rules: Name the output format (for example JSON with named fields).
Say what to do when information is missing.
Keep one task per request.
prompt_style.example: Extract the order items from this voice-note transcript and return JSON with customer, items (name, quantity) and delivery_date. Use null for anything not mentioned.

best_for: Builders who need reading, writing, extraction or planning inside their own app.
not_for: Audio transcription (use Muse Voice Transcribe) or image generation (use Muse Image).
unknowns: Rate limits for your account tier.
api_snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_MODEL_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1")
response = client.responses.create(model="muse-spark-1.3", input="Your prompt here")
print(response.output_text)
pricing_notes: Standard: $1.25/M input, $0.15/M cached, $4.25/M output. Contributor: $0.10/$0.002/$0.20 (Meta uses data to improve products). Per-token, no minimums.

pricing_model.quote: Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API

name: Muse Wonder
tagline: Meta's most capable model on the API, in preview.
summary: Meta's frontier API model (muse-wonder-1.0) for coding, long-running agents and computer use, with 1M context. Wonder Full, the stronger variant, is Muse Code subscription-only.
how_it_helps: Use it for harder planning and coding tasks where a stronger model is worth the extra cost, once you have confirmed access.
pros: Meta's frontier API model for coding, long-running agents and computer use.
Plans long tasks, delegates to sub-agents and recovers from errors.
Called through the same API and SDK as Muse Spark.
cons: Most expensive API model at $4 input / $20 output per 1M tokens.
Wonder Full, the stronger variant, needs a Muse Code subscription.
Confirm regional availability for your account.

prompt_style.technique: Give the goal, the constraints and the definition of done.
prompt_style.format: A short brief followed by the relevant code or files.
rules: State constraints first.
Ask for a plan before code on large tasks.
Say how you will check the result.
prompt_style.example: Review this function for bugs. List each problem with the line it affects, then give a corrected version and one test for each fix.

best_for: Complex planning and coding tasks in a project you are building.
not_for: Simple extraction or drafting, where Muse Spark is the better starting point.
unknowns: Rate limits for your account tier.

pricing_model.quote: Build with a single model at $0.18/hour.

name: Muse Voice Transcribe
tagline: Speech-to-text model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Speech-to-text on the Model API (muse-voice-transcribe-1.0): multipart REST upload for recordings, WebSocket for live transcription. 25 languages, speaker labels, turn-level timestamps.
how_it_helps: Use it to turn voice notes, interviews or calls into text before another model extracts or summarises the content.
pros: Transcribe a whole recording with one multipart REST request.
Live transcription over WebSocket with partial transcripts.
Speaker attribution for 20+ speakers with turn-level timestamps.
cons: 25 supported languages; Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin are not among them.
Turn-level timestamps only - no word-level timestamps or confidence scores.
Realtime and file transcription share one budget: 256 concurrent streams, 16,000 per hour.

prompt_style.technique: No text prompt: send the audio file.
prompt_style.format: Audio file in, transcript text out.
rules: Send WAV audio for file transcription.
Pick a mode: PUSH_TO_TALK, ENDPOINTING or DIARIZATION.
Treat speaker labels as session-scoped, not identities.

best_for: Turning voice notes, interviews and calls into text for later processing.
not_for: Understanding or summarising audio directly; transcribe first, then use a text model.
unknowns: Maximum file size and recording length.
pricing_notes: $0.18 per audio hour ($3.00 per 1,000 min). No minimums.

pricing_model.quote: Segment Anything Model (SAM) per image or video frame segmented, with no minimums or upfront commitment

name: SAM 3.1
tagline: Meta's segmentation model, available on the Meta Model API.
summary: Segments images and video on the Model API (sam-3.1) via streaming Responses calls: name an object, get a box plus pixel-precise mask per match, with tracking across frames. Nothing to host.
how_it_helps: Use it to locate objects or regions in a picture, for example to count items, crop them, or highlight them for review.
pros: Detection, segmentation and tracking in one zero-shot call.
Same API key, billing and SDK as the Muse models.
Pairs with Muse Spark: Spark interprets the scene, SAM cuts the masks.
cons: Pathwise's taxonomy has no segmentation job, so this card is mapped to edit_image.
Output is geometry (boxes and masks), not captions or text answers.
Video requests are billed for at least 50 frames.

prompt_style.technique: Name one concrete object with a short noun phrase.
prompt_style.format: Image plus a short noun phrase; box and mask per match.
rules: One object type per request; send several requests for several types.
Use box or point prompts when you know the location.
Check masks before relying on them.
prompt_style.example: Send the photo with the text "product label".

best_for: Locating and outlining objects in images inside your own app.
not_for: Generating new images or describing a scene in prose.
pricing_notes: $2.50 per 1,000 images; $0.20 per 1,000 video frames (min 50 frames per request).

pricing_model.quote: Agentic image generation, grounded by search and priced for production volumes at $0.01/image.

name: Muse Image
tagline: Meta's image generation model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Agentic image generation and editing on the Model API (muse-image-1.0) via the Responses API: it reasons, grounds with built-in search, then renders. $0.01 per image.
how_it_helps: Use it to produce illustrations, product visuals or social graphics from a written description, inside your own app.
pros: Generation, editing and multi-turn refinement in one model.
Built-in search grounding at no extra charge.
Called as muse-image-1.0 through the same API and SDK.
cons: Responses API returns a reasoning summary too; images endpoints return only the image.
Passing a web_search tool errors - search is built in and on by default.
Confirm regional availability for your account.

rules: Name the subject first.
Add style and lighting.
State the aspect ratio if it matters.
prompt_style.example: A clean product photo of a handmade soap bar on a white background, soft side light, square format.

best_for: Generating visuals from text inside a product you are building.
not_for: Workflows needing visibility into intermediate steps (lookups are not surfaced).
unknowns: Rate limits for your account tier.

name: Muse Code
summary: Meta's terminal coding agent with multi-agent coding. Flat-rate subscriptions (4 plans) or pay-as-you-go API billing; subscribing needs a Meta Account and age 18+.

pros: Flat-rate subscription option instead of per-token billing.
CLI onboarding auto-connects a Muse Code API key.
Docs include a cookbook, workflow guides and configuration reference.
cons: Subscription benefits and availability vary by region.
You must be 18 or older to subscribe.
API keys created outside the CLI are billed pay-as-you-go.

prompt_style.technique: Set ground rules first, then give one small task at a time.
prompt_style.format: A short instruction naming the files to touch and how to check the result.
rules: Ask it to inspect the repo before editing.
Give one task per prompt.
Ask for a report of files changed and tests run.
prompt_style.example: Inspect the project first. Add a Meta filter to the tools list, change only the files needed, run the tests and report what changed.

best_for: Developers who want an agent that edits a local project from the terminal.
not_for: Non-technical users who want a no-code builder.
pricing_notes: Flat monthly subscription (4 plans) or pay-as-you-go API billing; benefits vary by region.
